questions.question: Which formula defines the statistical distance (total variation) between PMFs P and Q?
questions.explanation: Statistical distance is one-half the L1 distance between the PMFs. The 1/2 aligns it with max_E |P(E) - Q(E)|.

questions.question: What is the range of `SD(P, Q)`?
questions.explanation: SD ∈ [0, 1]. It is 0 iff P = Q and 1 iff their supports are disjoint.

questions.question: Which equivalent characterization of SD makes its operational meaning explicit?
questions.explanation: SD equals the maximum, over all events E, of |P(E) - Q(E)|. This is exactly the best distinguishing advantage of an unbounded adversary.

questions.question: If `SD(P, Q) ≤ ε`, what does this say about any distinguisher D?
options: Its advantage |Pr[D=1|P] - Pr[D=1|Q]| is at most ε
Its runtime is at most ε
It outputs the correct distribution with probability at least 1-ε
Its advantage is exactly ε for the optimal D
questions.explanation: SD upper-bounds every distinguisher's advantage, regardless of computational power. The optimal unbounded D achieves advantage equal to SD.

questions.question: What is `SD(Bern(1/2 + ε), Bern(1/2))` for ε ∈ [-1/2, 1/2]?
questions.explanation: The biased and fair bits differ by |ε| on each outcome; halving the L1 sum gives SD = |ε|.

questions.question: Which property of SD makes hybrid arguments possible?
options: Triangle inequality: SD(P, Q) ≤ SD(P, R) + SD(R, Q)
Monotonicity: SD(P, Q) ≥ SD(P, R) for any R
Multiplicativity: SD(P × P', Q × Q') = SD(P, Q) · SD(P', Q')
Linearity: SD(αP + (1-α)Q, R) = α · SD(P, R) + (1-α) · SD(Q, R)
questions.explanation: The triangle inequality lets us chain distances across intermediate hybrids H_0, H_1, ..., H_k and sum the per-hop SDs.

questions.question: Why does SD only bound *unbounded* distinguishers, not all practical attacks on PRGs?
options: PRGs have large statistical distance from uniform but small computational distance
PRGs are deterministic, so SD does not apply
SD only works on finite distributions
PRGs use cryptographic hashes, which break statistical analysis
questions.explanation: A PRG's image is a tiny subset of {0,1}^n, so SD(PRG output, uniform) is essentially 1. PRG security is computational, not statistical.

questions.question: Which event E maximises `|P(E) - Q(E)|` and witnesses SD(P, Q)?
questions.explanation: The optimal distinguisher accepts exactly the outcomes where P puts more mass than Q. The resulting advantage equals SD.
